# DO NOT EDIT: generated from the MCP prompt of the same name.
name: deploy-and-test-class
description: "Deploys an ObjectScript class or package from local source files to IRIS with a glob-path load and compile, fixes compile errors in the source and loads it again, runs its unit tests, compares the returned total with the number of test methods because an early partial result looks like a green run, re-attaches to a run that is still going instead of starting a second one, and measures line coverage when the user asks for it. Use when the user wants to deploy, load or import ObjectScript source into IRIS, compile it, run its %UnitTest tests, or see their coverage."
metadata:
  iris-tools-preset: developer

# Deploy And Test Class

Target: `<classOrPackage>`

1. Deploy: call `iris_doc_load` with a **glob-prefixed path** rooted at the local source directory this class/package lives under, e.g. `c:/path/to/src/**/<classOrPackage>*.cls` — a bare (non-glob) file path derives an unqualified class name and the upload is REFUSED when it disagrees with the file's own Class declaration, so ALWAYS include a directory prefix ending in `**/*.cls` or `**/<ClassName>.cls`. Pass `compile: true`.
2. If the response reports compile errors, read each error's document/line/message, fix the SOURCE `.cls` file on disk (never edit generated/compiled output), and re-run step 1. A class that has no local source file (it exists only in IRIS) is fixed in place instead: read the reported lines with a ranged `iris_doc_get` (`startLine`/`endLine`), change them with `iris_doc_edit` (`action: "apply"`, each edit's `expected` built from the read's lines with every line followed by a line break), and run `iris_doc_compile` on the class (the `edit-and-test-class` prompt walks that loop). Repeat until `iris_doc_load` (or `iris_doc_compile`, for a class fixed in place) reports zero compile errors.
3. Determine the test level: if `<classOrPackage>` names a single class ending in a recognizable test-class pattern (or the user says "just this class"), use `level: "class"`; if it names a package, use `level: "package"`; if the user names one specific test method, use `level: "method"` with `target: "ClassName:MethodName"`.
4. Call `iris_execute_tests` with `target: "<classOrPackage>"` and the chosen `level`. If the response is a `PRODUCTION_BUSY` refusal, nothing ran. When the refusal has a `production` field, that production is running in the namespace and is not the tests' own: tell the user, and do not stop that production unless the user confirms it is a leftover of an interrupted test run. When its `state` is `Unknown`, the namespace's production state could not be read (the refusal says why): tell the user, run the tests again in a moment, and do not stop any production to make them run.
5. **If the response has `status: "running"` (`isError: false`), the run has NOT finished — do NOT treat it as a result and do NOT re-submit the same target** (that starts a second concurrent run against shared fixtures). Its top-level `total` does not exist; only `partial.total` does, and that is a drained-so-far subset, never a final count. Re-attach instead: call `iris_test_status` with `action: "poll"`, the response's `jobId` (and/or `runIndex`) and its `namespace` — it builds the SAME shapes from `%UnitTest_Result` authoritatively once finished. If `iris_test_status` is hidden under your current tool-visibility preset, the manual route in the response's `hint` still works: the `runIndex` (the response's own, or `iris_global_get` on `IRIS.TempAtelierAsyncQueue(<jobId>,"unittest","id")`), then `iris_sql_query` (with `parameters: [<runIndex>]`) joining `%UnitTest_Result.TestMethod` → `TestCase` → `TestSuite` → `TestInstance` `WHERE ti.InstanceIndex = ?` (only `TestInstance` has that column; never `MAX(InstanceIndex)`) — those rows exist while the run is still executing, so treat them as final only once `TestInstance.DateTime` (the hint's `FinishedAt`) is non-empty.
6. Otherwise, **compare the returned `total` against the expected number of test methods** (count them from the source file(s) you just deployed, or ask the user). `iris_execute_tests` can return an early PARTIAL snapshot — all passing, fewer tests than exist — which looks identical to a genuine green run unless the count is checked.
7. If `total` is short of the expected count, rerun `iris_execute_tests` (prefer a per-class call when precision matters; raise `timeout` if the suite is simply slow) before reporting the run as green.
8. Optional — line coverage, only when the user asks how much of the code the tests cover or gives a coverage target, and once the tests pass: call `iris_test_coverage` with the same `target` and `level`, `classes` set to the classes the tests exercise (not the test classes; at most 50), and `minCoverage` set to the user's target when there is one. It runs the tests again under an instance-wide line monitor. If `iris_test_coverage` is not in your tool list, the tool-visibility preset hides it (it is outside `core`): tell the user it needs the `developer` or full preset (`IRIS_TOOLS_PRESET`), and report the results without coverage. If it is refused with `GOVERNANCE_DISABLED`, it is disabled by default because it starts an instance-wide monitor and runs test code: tell the user the operator can enable it through `IRIS_GOVERNANCE`, for example `{"global":{"iris_test_coverage":true}}`, report the results without coverage, and do not measure coverage another way. If it is refused with `MONITOR_BUSY`, another monitor session is running on the instance (its `owner` says whose) and nothing was started: tell the user, and never stop that session. If it is refused with `PRODUCTION_BUSY`, handle it as in step 4. If the response has `status: "running"`, do NOT re-submit: call `iris_test_status` with `action: "poll"` and the response's `coverageRunId` until it completes. Report each class's percent and uncovered line ranges and, with `minCoverage`, the verdict (a failing verdict is a result, not a tool error). A class reported `not-up-to-date` after a documentation-only edit (a comment or a `///` line) needs a forced compile before it can be measured: call `iris_doc_compile` on it with `flags: "ck"`, then call `iris_test_coverage` again. For a Cobertura file, call `iris_test_status` with `action: "export"`, the `coverageRunId` and an absolute `outputPath` ending in `.xml` that the user chose (for example `c:/path/to/coverage.xml`); export is disabled by default too (`iris_test_status:export`), so handle a `GOVERNANCE_DISABLED` refusal the same way.
9. Report the final pass/fail/skipped counts and any failure details to the user, and the coverage, when it was measured.
